clue.text: Very economical price had struggling stores close to debt

indicators.note: to store something is to hold it inside, so the jumble keeps the next letter within it
letters that are struggling are in disarray, so the words price had get rearranged
the close of a word is its final letter, here taken from debt

explanation.surface: A shopper notes that a cheap price came from a struggling chain of stores nearly in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges PRICE HAD, which 'stores' the T that ends 'debt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dirt cheap costs almost nothing, so it is very economical.

clue.text: Keep order to pay £1,000 a long time

parts.note: to dun someone is to demand payment of a debt
a grand, abbreviated G, is a thousand pounds
an eon is an immeasurably long period

explanation.surface: A creditor demands a thousand pounds and is prepared to wait an age for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the strongest tower of a castle, and a dungeon in the old sense is that same donjon.

clue.text: Drug trial failed with it

indicators.note: a failed trial has fallen apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: being with it means fashionable, which is IN

explanation.surface: A clinical test of a medicine went wrong, and the drug was involved.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a brand of methylphenidate, a stimulant medication prescribed for ADHD.

clue.text: Lament delay, netting a pound where fortune's sought

parts.note: to lament is to cry

indicators.note: a net catches and holds, so STALL holds the next pieces inside

parts.note: to stall is to play for time
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Someone grieves over a hold-up that has cost them a pound, at a fortune-teller's booth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'netting' means the delay word is split open to hold the other pieces; 'pound' here is the weight abbreviation, not sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune-teller gazes into a glass sphere to read what the future holds.

clue.text: Lacking mates, having day off that's tediously long

indicators.note: a day off is taken away, so these letters drop out of the longer word

parts.note: with no friends at all is friendless
Fri is the abbreviation for Friday

explanation.surface: A lonely person with a day off finds the hours drag on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having day off' removes FRI from the start of FRIENDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that seems to have no end drags on tediously.

clue.text: Photo frames hang on synthetic material

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so these letters sit around the next piece

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo
to hang on is to endure or last

explanation.surface: A photograph is mounted in a frame made of some artificial substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastics are man-made polymers, the classic synthetic substance.

clue.text: 25 11's wrong, stifling way of working

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so the wrong wraps around the way of working

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
MO is modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: A TV personality is accused of being wrong and suppressing a working method.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references give Cowell, the TV talent-show judge; the answer is his first name. 'stifling' marks the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Cowell is the music mogul and TV talent-show judge, so his first name fits.

clue.text: Old man's unfinished title

indicators.note: not finished means the last letter is lost

parts.note: a sire is a father, an old man in slang

explanation.surface: Dad has never quite completed the honour he was promised.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the form of address used for a knight or baronet.

clue.text: He makes a killing beginning to market gold stocks a bit

indicators.note: to stock is to hold in store, so the outer letters keep the next piece inside
the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken from market

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a tad is a small bit

explanation.surface: A trader profits hugely when stocks of gold rise a little early in the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocks' marks the container. The financial surface of 'makes a killing' hides a literal killer in the bullring.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter's job is to kill the bull in the ring.

clue.text: London university splitting noble gas particle

indicators.note: splitting something breaks it open, so the university goes inside the gas

parts.note: neon is an inert or noble gas
UCL is University College London

explanation.surface: Scientists at a London university split atoms of a rare gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A proton or neutron in an atom's core is called by this name, a subatomic particle.

clue.text: Like muesli and bananas?

definitions.meaning: muesli contains nuts, so it tastes of them

explanation.surface: A breakfast question: is it like muesli with fruit in it?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both full of nuts and, informally, mad.

clue.text: Maybe grave judge backs withdrawing help

indicators.note: the judge backs, or stands behind, the other piece
to withdraw is to draw back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: aid is help
a critic judges works

explanation.surface: A solemn judge supports pulling out of an aid programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' gives DIA; 'backs' puts the judge behind it. 'grave' looks like serious, but it is the accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave accent is one example of a mark added to a letter to show pronunciation.

clue.text: Distance fellow travellers cover repeatedly

indicators.note: the two words each cover, or conceal, the same short run of letters, so it is found twice

explanation.surface: Comrades on a journey cover a long distance again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in both 'fellow' and 'travellers', hence 'repeatedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old English measure of length, about forty-five inches, used for cloth.

clue.text: First of Tests and opening game could be here

definitions.text: First of Tests and opening game could be here

indicators.note: the first of a word is its initial letter, taken from Tests

parts.note: a rent is a gap or opening
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A cricket ground where the first Test of the series might open.
explanation.walkthrough: Trent Bridge is the Test cricket ground in Nottingham, England; a Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: This Nottingham venue regularly hosts Test matches, sometimes the opening game of a series.

clue.text: Conservative, behind May's back, keeps fighting

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the behind holds the fighting inside

parts.note: the rear is the behind
action is combat or fighting

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, taken from May

explanation.surface: A Tory politician stands behind Theresa May while fighting on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' marks the container; 'May's back' adds a final Y. Theresa May was the Conservative Prime Minister, a deliberate distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A reactionary opposes progress and wants to keep things as they were, a right-wing outlook.

clue.text: Puzzle not having a positive value?

parts.note: non- is a prefix meaning not
a plus quantity is a positive one

explanation.surface: A maths riddle: what is a number that is not positive?
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to perplex them so they do not know what to do.

clue.text: Romeo tucked into two drinks, in distress

indicators.note: the letter is tucked into, placed inside, the drinks

parts.note: cha is tea and gin is a spirit
R is Romeo in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo downs a couple of drinks, being heartbroken.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside CHA + GIN. 'tucked into' also suggests eating, but it marks the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation or annoyed embarrassment, a form of distress.

clue.text: Traveller's plane took off ahead of time

indicators.note: the preceding pieces come before the next one

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
to take off is to run away, so ran

explanation.surface: A traveller's flight departed early.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrant is someone who moves from place to place, a traveller.

clue.text: Fellows wearing ladies' slippers and cloaks

indicators.note: the slippers are worn on the outside, round the fellows

parts.note: mules are backless slippers worn by women
F is fellow, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Men dressed in women's slippers and capes.
explanation.definitionFit: To muffle is to wrap up or conceal, the verb sense of cloak.

clue.text: More frivolous Greek admits: "That would be the end of me"

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the abbreviation holds the next piece

parts.words: That would be the end of me
parts.note: spoken as I'd die, my death

explanation.surface: A light-hearted Greek confesses something would be the death of him.
explanation.definitionFit: Giddy means flighty and frivolous, so the comparative is more frivolous.

clue.text: Eatery's charge low, needing to rise

parts.note: to tear is to rush, to charge

indicators.note: in a down light a rising word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a cow lows, it moos

explanation.surface: A café's prices are low and need to go up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing to rise' reverses MOO to OOM. 'charge' and 'low' look like prices, but are rush and cow-noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea room is a small café serving light meals, so a kind of eatery.

clue.text: Stand a bit of laughter and song

parts.note: ha is a single laugh
a track is one song on an album

explanation.surface: Someone can tolerate a little laughing and singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatstand is a piece of furniture for hanging hats, the same thing.

clue.text: Husband experiences lust problems

parts.note: to itch for something is to crave it

explanation.surface: A married man's desires cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitches are snags or difficulties, a synonym of problems.

clue.text: Car with uneven bulge able to be picked up

parts.note: Audi is a German car make

indicators.note: the uneven, odd-numbered letters of bulge are taken

explanation.surface: A car with a lopsided dent can be lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uneven' picks letters 1, 3 and 5 of 'bulge'. 'picked up' looks like lifted, but means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound that can be heard is audible; picked up is used of a signal or noise detected.

clue.text: Equipment sent for tidying up litter

parts.note: kit is equipment

indicators.note: tidying moves things around, so the letters of sent are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gear was sent to clean up rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' looks like rubbish but means a brood of young cats.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's brood born together is a litter, and its members are young cats.

clue.text: Dog guzzling claret's drunk an old red

indicators.note: guzzling takes something in, so the dog holds the next piece

parts.note: Fido is a traditional dog's name

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady, so the letters of claret's are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, letters CLARETS

explanation.surface: A dog laps up spilt claret, being an old red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' gives the jumble ELCASTR, which 'guzzling' puts inside the dog's name before its last letter. 'red' looks like wine, but means communist.
explanation.definitionFit: Castro led communist Cuba for decades; red is slang for a communist.

clue.text: I may have one day by Ruth or Daniel's place

parts.note: both books are in the Old Testament, OT

explanation.surface: Someone hopes for a day out at a biblical site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the letter, not the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A lower-case i carries a small point above it, the tittle.

clue.text: Look inside church, securing good deal for organ cover

parts.note: lo is an old word for look
in means inside

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the church holds the deal

parts.note: a lot is a good deal

explanation.surface: Peer into a church where someone is clinching a deal on the organ's covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the church instrument but is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth worn around the hips covers the genitals, a body organ.

clue.text: Intimidate businesswomen?

definitions.meaning: read as business, CO, plus women, W: a company of women

explanation.surface: Do female executives bully people?
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to frighten them into submission; the second reading splits into company and women.

clue.text: Walker's nude walk

indicators.note: nude means stripped, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: a rambler is a hiker

explanation.surface: A hiker goes for a naked stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to stroll at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: Way to get untreated stable bed?

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
raw means unprocessed

explanation.surface: How to get a natural bed for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses are bedded down on dried stalks in their stalls.

clue.text: Problem about marketing, eg for Greens

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a sum is a maths problem
hype is aggressive marketing
as means for example

explanation.surface: An issue around promoting environmentalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses SUM. Mushy peas are a British side dish of mashed marrowfat peas, served with fish and chips. 'Greens' suggests politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: These are green vegetables, so they count as greens.
